links.outcome: Complex multimodal fusion versus simpler EHR-alone baseline on discrimination
links.effect: No fusion architecture significantly outperformed EHR-alone (ROC-AUC 0.63); removing auxiliary modalities improved rather than degraded fusion performance under stress testing.
links.quote: No fusion architecture significantly outperformed the EHR-alone baseline (ROC-AUC 0.63); removing auxiliary modalities improved rather than degraded fusion performance under stress testing.

links.outcome: Calibration and Brier score of EHR-alone versus fusion, with and without recalibration
links.effect: Raw Brier was about 0.24 for fusion versus 0.32 for EHR-alone, reflecting EHR-alone overconfidence (calibration slope 0.12); after recalibration Brier scores were indistinguishable (0.239 vs 0.240-0.244).
links.quote: The raw Brier score was lower for all three fusion architectures than for EHR-alone (about 0.24 versus 0.32), but this reflected overconfidence of the EHR-alone probe (calibration slope 0.12); after logistic recalibration fitted on the validation set, Brier scores were indistinguishable (EHR-alone 0.239; fusion 0.240-0.244; all paired bootstrap 95% CIs included zero).
